newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Bosnia seeks to open border crossing - official.
newsitem.headline: Bosnia seeks to open border crossing - official.

text.p: Ministers in Bosnia's central cabinet have agreed to enter negotiations with Croatia about opening the country's northern border to restore trade links, the office for the international High Representative to Bosnia said on Friday.
"They have agreed to open negotiations on the subject of opening the border," Colum Murphy, a spokesman for the High Representative's office, told Reuters.
The Council of Ministers, the peacetime central cabinet, discussed opening at least one crossing on the northern border at its session on Thursday, he said.

"The initiative to open more border crossings was absolutely supported, but we have to agree with Croatia about the locations," Boro Bosic, the Serb co-chairman of of the council, told state radio on Thursday.
"We expect this task to be finished soon," Bosic said.

Bosnia's northern border crossings with Croatia have been closed or severely restricted since war erupted in former Yugoslavia in 1991, when Croatia declared independence from Serbian-dominated Yugoslavia.
The northern border straddles Bosnia's autonomous Serb territory, which covers half the country.
Businessmen and farmers in the northwest Banja Luka region have pleaded for the border to be reopened to restore traditional trade links.

Bosnian Serb authorities had been reluctant to allow a free flow of goods across the border with Croatia, partly because of lingering mistrust from the war and partly because they wanted to retain a monopoly on imported goods through state-controlled firms, economic analysts said.

But Serb authorities are facing severe fiscal pressures, owing wages to public employees and six months worth of pension payments. Opening the border to trade would bring in badly needed hard currency and customs revenues, analysts said.
